name: Infiniti Q50 3.7
reliability: 7/10 — durable VQ V6; watch oil consumption and warping brake rotors
popular_mods: Cold air intake, headers, catback exhaust (modest NA gains)
Note: naturally aspirated — gains are modest vs the turbo VR30 cars

generations.2014 (Launch): Debuted at 2013 NAIAS. Replaced the G37. Introduced Direct Adaptive Steering (steer-by-wire). 3.7L VQ37VHR and Hybrid (354hp) available.
generations.2015: Final year of the 3.7L engine. Minor refinements. Last chance to get the naturally aspirated V6 in the Q50.

common_issues: Valve train noise — often quieted with Nissan ester oil
Rear timing cover gasket leak (oil pressure stresses paper gasket)
Oil consumption from worn valve seals or piston rings at high mileage
maintenance_tips: Use Nissan genuine ester oil to reduce valve train noise
Inspect rear timing cover for oil seepage at 60k+ miles
Check oil level every fill-up — engine can consume oil silently

engine.detail: 3.7L VQ37VHR naturally aspirated V6 — 328 hp at 7,000 rpm and 269 lb-ft, with Nissan's VVEL (Variable Valve Event and Lift) on the intake and a 7,500-rpm redline. The last naturally aspirated engine offered in the Q50, and a proven, high-revving unit.
engine.watch: Valve-train noise (a top-end tick) is common and usually quiets down on Nissan's genuine ester oil. Watch for the rear timing-cover gasket weeping oil under pressure at 60k+, and for oil consumption from worn valve seals or rings on higher-mile cars — check the level every fill-up.

drivetrain.detail: Jatco-built 7-speed automatic (JR711E) driving the rear wheels, or Infiniti's Intelligent AWD that only sends torque forward when the rears start to slip.
drivetrain.watch: Durable behind the NA V6. Don't trust the 'lifetime fill' claim — fresh ATF every 30-40k is cheap insurance.

suspension.detail: Double-wishbone front and multi-link rear. The 2014 Q50 debuted Direct Adaptive Steering (DAS) — a steer-by-wire system with no mechanical link between the wheel and rack in normal driving (a clutch mechanically re-couples them if it faults); non-DAS cars kept a conventional rack.
suspension.watch: DAS is the enthusiast sore point — steering feel is numb and artificial with little genuine road feedback. On high-mile cars, refresh bushings and dampers; coilovers and sway bars are the usual first upgrades.

brakes.detail: Vented front and solid rear discs with ABS and stability control.
brakes.watch: Rotor warping (a pulsation through the pedal under braking) is the noted weak point — quality replacement rotors/pads and fresh fluid cure it.

body.detail: Steel unibody sport sedan at about 3,574 lbs, with Infiniti's dual-screen InTouch infotainment inside.
body.watch: Typical age items — rock chips, trim and seal wear; the older InTouch system can feel laggy by modern standards.
